nodes.summary: The Weierstrass function $W(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} \cos(160^k x) / 4^k$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Continuity of the Weierstrass function

nodes.summary: For every real number $c$ and every positive integer $K$, there is a real number $y$ with $c + \pi / K < y < c + 3\pi / K$ such that $|\cos(Kc) - \cos(Ky)| \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Cosine oscillation (scaled form)

nodes.summary: For every real number $\theta$ there is a real number $\varphi$ with $\pi < \varphi < 3\pi$ such that $|\cos\theta - \cos(\theta + \varphi)| \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Cosine oscillation (phase-shift form)

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$ and every real number $x$, $|\cos(160^k x) / 4^k| \le (1/4)^k$.
nodes.title: Termwise bound for the Weierstrass series

nodes.summary: For all real numbers `a`, `b`, `c`, the absolute value of their sum is at least `|a| - |b| - |c|`.
nodes.title: Reverse triangle inequality, three terms

nodes.summary: For every real number $x$, the series $\sum_{k \ge 0} \cos(160^k x) / 4^k$ defining the Weierstrass function converges absolutely, that is, $\sum_{k \ge 0} |\cos(160^k x) / 4^k|$ is summable.
nodes.title: Absolute convergence of the Weierstrass series

nodes.summary: For every real number $x$, the series $\sum_{k \ge 0} \cos(160^k x) / 4^k$ defining the Weierstrass function is summable, by comparison with the geometric series $\sum_{k \ge 0} (1/4)^k$.
nodes.title: Summability of the Weierstrass series

nodes.summary: The Weierstrass function $W(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} \cos(160^k x) / 4^k$ satisfies $|W(x)| \le 4/3$ for every real number $x$.
nodes.title: Bound on the Weierstrass function

nodes.summary: The Weierstrass function $W(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \cos(160^k x) / 4^k$ is differentiable at no point of $\mathbb{R}$: for every real number $c$, $W$ is not differentiable at $c$.
nodes.title: The Weierstrass function is nowhere differentiable

nodes.summary: For every real `c` and every natural number `n`, there exists a point `y ≠ c` with `|y - c| < 3π / 160ⁿ` such that the difference quotient of the Weierstrass function between `y` and `c` has absolute value at least `40ⁿ / (117 π)`. Since `40ⁿ / (117 π) → ∞`, this witnesses that the function cannot have a finite derivative at `c`.
nodes.title: Slope blow-up lemma

nodes.summary: The Weierstrass function is the function $W : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ given by $W(x) = \sum_{k \ge 0} \cos(160^k x) / 4^k$, the sum running over all natural numbers $k$.
nodes.title: The Weierstrass function

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
